correct_completion: she sent it to her manager.
full_sentence: Having finished the report, she sent it to her manager.
acceptable_variants: she handed it in before lunch.
she printed copies for the team.

options.text: the report was sent to her manager.
options.why_wrong: This makes the report the grammatical subject, which conflicts with the participle clause that refers to 'she'.

options.text: she was sent a new report.
options.why_wrong: This changes the action to receiving a report, so 'Having finished' no longer leads to a logical result.

options.text: she sent it to her manager.

options.why_wrong: This repeats the completed action of the participle clause instead of giving the main action that follows it.

grammar_focus: Perfect participle clauses ('Having + past participle') with a shared subject
explanation: A perfect participle clause describes an action completed before the main action, and its implied subject must match the subject of the main clause.
translation: Habiendo terminado el informe, ella lo envió a su jefe.
